content.text:
The pattern points to orthorhombic PrFeO3 (mp-22341) as the one phase present, but the fit is poor, so my confidence is only moderate.

- **Cubic perovskites ruled out:** BaScO3 and BaSrZrSnO6 fit badly (R about 0.99). Even at their best strain, their strongest line sits about 2° below the observed strongest peak near 31.7°, so they can't reach it.
- **Best single fit:** PrFeO3 gives the lowest R of the four I tried, 0.83, at −0.5 % strain. CaHfO3 fits worse (R 0.91) and needed the full −2 % strain limit. I did not fit LiMn3O4, Ba2ErCoCu2O7, Li5Co3O8, LiNiO2 or Rb5Au3O2.
- **Why the fit is still weak:** after the PrFeO3 fit, the residual has a peak of about 36 at the main reflection, with negative dips on both sides. That shape suggests the peak positions are slightly off, not a missing phase. The data are also very noisy.
- **No second phase:** adding CaHfO3 only lowered R from 0.83 to 0.81. It again sat at the −2 % strain limit, so it looks like it is just patching the main-peak misfit, not a real phase. I left it out, and it remains the most likely alternative if a second phase were present.
